recipes.name: Cilantro Lime Salad Dressing
ingredients_raw: 1 medium jalapeno pepper, seeded and coarsely chopped

steps.text: Pulse jalapeño, garlic, and ginger in a food processor until finely chopped. Add honey, lime juice, cilantro, vinegar, and salt. Pulse 3 to 4 times to blend.
Slowly pour oil into the processor with the motor running until dressing is smooth. Taste and season with salt if needed before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cilantro Lime Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Inspired by the delicious dressing on the grilled chicken salad at TGI Fridays, I created my own version. Drizzle it on anything that needs more flavor.

review.reviewBody: OH MY GOODNESS!!! This dressing really is that yummy! I always get rave reviews when I make it, and everyone asks for the recipe. My husbands eyes light up when I tell him that we are having out Southwest Chicken salad for dinner with this dressing. It is way better than anything you can buy in the store. We do add a little less honey like others have stated. You can add a little more lime if you want it to be a little more tangy, or a little more vinegar for more of a vinegarette flavor. One time I put about 4x the vinegar (on accident) and it still tasted great. We just put the whole thing in our Vita-mix blender in the order it is written and blend it up - it turns out great that way, and you don't have to chop everything. For our Southwest salad we do 1-2 heads of lettuce, 2 cobs of raw white corn kernels, 1 large can of black beans rinsed, 1 bag of Montery Jack cheese, 1 red onion, grilled chicken breast, and 1 bunch of cilantro. We have also added tomatoes and avocado if you like them. Thank you to the poster of this recipe, you did a great job!
Delicious. I put 1/8 of a cup of honey and it was still too sweet. I recommend blending everything and adding a tiny bit of honey at a time.

Overall, it is a good dressing. The flavor is good. However, it is very sweet. I was looking for a strong cilantro lime flavor and there is just a hint of it here and there. Next time I make it, I will use 1 Tbsp honey, swap the Balsamic vinegar for extra lime juice, add more ginger, and double the cilantro. I also used like 7 cloves of garlic bc what even is 1 garlic clove? This is just my personal preference, but the recipe is a good recipe if you like sweet dressing.

6-21-20 ~This was one of the best, most memorable, dressings I’ve made in a very long time. Thank goodness for a couple of things – first, that Hubs was out of town as anything with cilantro must be avoided as far as he’s concerned. Second, that it was the rare occasion I had some ginger on hand. This dressing would never have come to pass without these factors. I have to say that the ginger and the balsamic vinegar kind of threw me here and I questioned how they’d work in a cilantro-lime dressing. It turns out that while neither is boldly evident, they are indispensable ingredients that create a well-balanced, nuanced whole. I made one simple adjustment, reducing the honey by half, to suit my tastes and, for me, that was perfect. I drizzled this over butter lettuce topped with grilled chicken, seasoned simply with salt, pepper and a little garlic powder so as not to compete with this totally fresh and lovely dressing.

Looked this up after eating a wonderful Salad dressed with something like this at a high end Mexican restaurant in Asheville. I subtracted the balsamic, eliminated the ollive oil, and substituted a more neutral (grapeseed) oil to allow the delicate lime/cilantro to stand out. Why would you want to use balsamic on a Mexican inspired mixture? Also I added coriander (fresh ground) since coriander and cilantro are natural together. Came out light and fresh just like I had on my salad. Almost better.

This is delicious - I plan on making this a lot and eating it on EVERYTHING!! I did some adjusting with salt and lime juice but basically stuck to the recipe. You have to let it sit a while for the flavours to marry. I marinated tofu in the dressing and served it on quinoa, black beans, tomato, cucumber & red onion. Also mixed it with some vegan cream cheese and used it as a dip, and ate it on its own with potato patties.I could seriously drink this stuff. Just go make it already!!!

I gave this 3 stars as it is because it's way too sweet with that much honey, but I cut the honey back to 1 Tbsp and it's 5 stars. I make this and toss it with coleslaw mix and serve it with fish tacos--delicious!!
One of our favorite homemade dressings. If you use cilantro paste no chopping or blending required, although fresh cilantro is great as well

The base ingredient mix of this recipe is nice; however, we found it too sweet for our liking. Next time I make it, I will do as others suggested and use 1/4 honey, 1/3 cup lime juice and double the cilantro. We like things a little spicy so I will add in more jalapeño as that background heat was really nice. Good recipe, you just need to adapt the measurements to your liking.

This will definitely be one of my go to recipes. So versatile. I drizzled over shredded chicken to make tacos; used when I cooked white rice for cilantro lime rice. The only change I made was to add two, yes 2 bunches of cilantro. I am a cilantro addict but I actually changed the recipe for 30 servings. Overall 2 thumbs up and a high five!

Great recipe, I made and then I made it again. I did not like the balsamic vinegar or how sweet it was. 
This is what I changed and it is terrific!
2-jalapeño, 2-clove garlic, 3/4 - ginger, the juice of 1 1/2-2 - limes, 1 1/2 -2 tsp white sugar, 2-tsp white wine vinegar, 1/2- salt, 1/2 - cup of cilantro leaves, 1/3-1/2 cup of extra virgin olive oil or same amount of avocado oil. Then mix as above. Love it, thank you

This is my new favorite dressing! All my favorite ingredients in one dish. The first time I made it, it was bitter. Perhaps from pulsing the olive oil too long, so I added a touch more honey and it was fine. This time it was perfection, maybe a tad too sweet so I’ll cut the honey a few tablespoons next time. My only disappointment was I hadn’t tried it sooner.

I agree with others that it is really sweet. I only had a couple of tablespoons of honey left andstill added more lime juice and cilantro to bring back those flavors. Also, even with 1/3 cup of honey, I don't see how you will get 2 cupds of dressing. Is there a wet ingredient missing?

I followed the recipe as is, and it came out extremely sweet. Also, 87 (!) per serving is not cool at all. I’d better make it without honey and then see if a very small amount is still necessary. Don’t use honey at all; it just makes it taste bad and overloaded with sugar.

I've been looking for a good cilantro lime dressing recipe and this is it! Just delicious. Several folks say the amount of honey makes it too sweet. It all depends on your preferences - I think it's great as is.
I didn’t measure but approximated not too far off. Creamy and delicious! Now I know what to do when I get a lot of cilantro all at once!
Very good—reduced the amount of olive oil slightly to cut calories a little

We eat a lot of salads, so I’m glad to find a new, really different dressing that we enjoyed. It was a salad for lunch this time, but next time, it’ll be with some shrimp on it as a main course. This is personal taste, but I’ll add more jalapeño in the future. There’s a really good sweet-sour balance between the vinegar-lime which is sweetened by the honey. And I like the nutritional breakdown on this.
Super easy in the blender, and tastes fantastic! Made our taco salad very special tonight!
It was awesome just as it is
